findings.reason: The protected SQL implementation joins Customers, Orders, and Product, filters orders to the June-July 2020 window ('2020-06-01' to '2020-08-01'), groups by customer, and uses conditional SUM CASE aggregations in HAVING to enforce >= 100 spending in June and >= 100 in July independently. The query is concise, optimal, and single-pass; no candidate is required.

The half-open date interval includes all June and July dates. The two conditional SUM CASE expressions evaluate quantity * price specifically for June (< '2020-07-01') and July (>= '2020-07-01') separately, and HAVING requires both totals to be >= 100 independently.

Joining C customers, P products, and O orders and grouping by customer takes O(C + P + O log O) time with sorting, or expected O(C + P + O) time with hash aggregation. Working space is O(C + P + O). Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Returns the exact required output columns customer_id and name, handles multi-unit purchases and multiple orders per month, and filters strictly by June and July independent thresholds.

The approach accurately details joining relations to compute monetary values, half-open interval date filtering, single-pass conditional aggregation in HAVING, and relational complexity bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover joining two monthly subqueries, correlated subqueries, combined threshold errors, exact 100 thresholds, multiple orders, missing months, and outside dates.
